subject.title: [Feature] Control UI should accept gateway token from Authorization header

question: Which reverse-proxy shared-secret bootstrap model should Control UI support for turning proxy-provided headers into WebSocket credentials?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the choice affects spoofing protections, trusted proxy requirements, browser origin handling, rate limits, pairing/device semantics, and credential lifetime.

options.title: Use a short-lived browser session
options.body: Validate Authorization or X-OpenClaw-Token on a same-origin bootstrap endpoint and mint a bounded browser credential for the WebSocket path.

options.title: Validate on WebSocket upgrade
options.body: Accept a purpose-built shared-secret header during trusted WebSocket upgrades after origin, proxy, and rate-limit checks.

options.title: Keep current auth paths
options.body: Decline shared-secret header bootstrap and keep connect.params auth plus identity-bearing Tailscale/trusted-proxy modes as the supported Control UI paths.

recommendation.title: Use a short-lived browser session
recommendation.body: Validate Authorization or X-OpenClaw-Token on a same-origin bootstrap endpoint and mint a bounded browser credential for the WebSocket path.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this exact issue and has the strongest recent Gateway HTTP/WebSocket auth-boundary history.
